entries.label: The Court
entries.description: Opens the Court, where disputes and petitions wait to be settled.

entries.label: Decrees
entries.description: Opens the Decrees panel, where standing orders are written to answer petitions without you.

entries.label: Crown charter
entries.description: Opens the Crown panel and starts the crown's demands. Governors, forging and conjuring all need it.

entries.label: Command palette
entries.description: Opens the command line empty, with every command you own listed as you type.

entries.label: Saved decrees
entries.description: Keep a decree under a name and enact it again later with one command.

entries.label: Compound conditions
entries.description: Join conditions in a decree with and, or and not.

entries.label: Chaining
entries.description: Let one decree react to the policy another decree chose.

entries.label: Crown correspondence
entries.description: Let decrees read what the crown still demands, as owedOre, owedWood, owedGrain and owedCoin.

entries.label: Exact books
entries.description: Shows debt to the decimal instead of rounded up to the nearest ten, and how long until announced auditors arrive. Decrees may also read debt.

entries.label: True reports
entries.description: Strips governors' exaggeration: the Ledger's rates count only what the stores really receive, and each governor is listed with their real output and the gap.

entries.label: Conjuring
entries.description: Lets you add grain or coin to the Ledger that the stores do not hold.

entries.label: Forging
entries.description: Lets you report a crown demand as delivered on paper, and owe the difference.

entries.label: Governors
entries.description: Lets candidates arrive on the Court's desk to be hired as governors.

entries.label: Granary
entries.description: A proper granary for the harvest, holding 400 more grain before the surplus spoils.

entries.label: Woodshed
entries.description: A roof and four walls for the timber, holding 300 more wood.

entries.label: Ore store
entries.description: A dry cellar for the ore, holding 150 more of it.

entries.label: Iron-shod ploughs
entries.description: Farmers coax a quarter more grain from the same field.

entries.label: Sharper axes
entries.description: Foresters fell a quarter more wood in a day.

entries.label: Stronger picks
entries.description: Miners bring up a quarter more ore, and break fewer picks doing it.

entries.label: Market rights
entries.description: The reeve may haggle in the market square, and sold goods fetch a quarter more.

entries.label: Petitions
entries.description: Peasants may bring requests to the Court, some of which are worth granting.

entries.label: Larger granary
entries.description: Another wing for the granary, holding 800 more grain.

entries.label: Larger woodshed
entries.description: A second shed, holding 600 more wood.

entries.label: Deeper ore store
entries.description: A deeper cellar, holding 300 more ore.

entries.label: Heavy ploughs
entries.description: Two oxen to the plough, and another quarter more grain from the field.

entries.label: Felling wedges
entries.description: Iron wedges and two-man saws, for another quarter more wood.

entries.label: Iron-bound props
entries.description: Timbered galleries let miners dig deeper, for another quarter more ore.

entries.label: Moneylender's favor
entries.description: A word to the moneylender, and debt grows by a third less each season.

entries.label: Friends at court
entries.description: A few gifts to the right clerks, and auditors wait half a season longer between visits.

entries.label: Court omens
entries.description: A seer takes a seat at the Court, and warns you of lean seasons for a fee.

entries.label: Great granary
entries.description: A granary the size of a cathedral, holding 1600 more grain.

entries.label: Great woodshed
entries.description: A timber yard under roof, holding 1200 more wood.

entries.label: Great ore store
entries.description: A vault cut into the hillside, holding 600 more ore.

entries.label: Village physician
entries.description: A learned man in every governor's village, who halves the chance that one dies in a season.

entries.label: Provincial seats
entries.description: The crown allows two more provinces to be given to governors.
